items.about: The first shot fades into the second while both overlap briefly. For gentle, neutral cuts in any film, vlog or interview.
The picture fades down to black, then the next shot fades up from black. For scene endings, time jumps and solemn moments.
The picture washes out to white, then the next shot fades in from white. For bright, dreamy or memory-like scene changes.
A warm orange-white glow sweeps left to right across the frame, brightest at the cut. For warm, golden cuts in travel or lifestyle videos.
A white-yellow burst of light grows from the center and whites out the cut. For energetic cuts on a beat or in a launch film.
An orange overexposed band runs across the frame like burnt film, hiding the cut. For nostalgic or analog-style cuts.
A flat off-white panel slides in from the left, covers the frame and exits right; the cut happens behind it. For clean, graphic cuts.
Black bars close from top and bottom to meet in the middle, then open onto the next shot. For crisp, cinematic scene changes.
A black circle closes in on the center of the frame, then opens again on the next shot. For classic, playful scene changes.
Vertical black stripes widen like window blinds until the frame is covered, then open again. For stylish scene changes.
Black ink blots spread from the middle and swallow the frame, then lift away over the next shot. For dramatic, artistic cuts.
A pink heart grows from the center until it fills the screen, then fades. For romantic, cute or wedding cuts.
A yellow star spins out from the center, covers the frame, then fades. For fun, celebratory or kids' cuts.
Pink and cyan bars with a dark frame jump sideways for a moment, like a broken signal. For techy, fast cuts.
A short burst of grey TV noise flickers over the frame and hides the cut. For retro, horror or channel-change cuts.
A moving film-grain noise lies over the whole picture and changes every frame. For an analog, filmic texture on any shot.
The corners of the picture are darkened toward black, with a clear center. For drawing the eye to the middle and a moodier look.
Thin white and dark vertical scratches jump across the picture, with a faint flicker. For old-film or silent-movie looks.
Fine dark horizontal lines run across the whole frame, like an old screen. For retro monitor, CRT or sci-fi looks.
Warm orange and pink light drifts in from the left and right edges, pulsing slowly. For warm, nostalgic or dreamy footage.
A bright sun-like flare sits in the top-right corner with faint colored spots, breathing slowly. For sunny, cinematic shots.
Soft pale rays fall from the top-left corner and slowly brighten and fade. For sunlight through trees, windows or a hopeful mood.
White snowflakes of three sizes fall and sway, the near ones larger and blurred. For winter, holiday or calm scenes.
Thin pale streaks fall fast at a slant across the frame. For rainy, sad or moody scenes.
Small pale-yellow four-pointed stars twinkle here and there across the frame. For magic, glamour or celebration.
Many small colored paper pieces tumble down the screen. For parties, wins, birthdays and announcements.
Pink cherry blossom petals drift down and sideways across the frame. For spring, romance, weddings and Asian-style scenes.
Clear round bubbles with white highlights rise from the bottom of the frame. For underwater, kids and playful scenes.
A white flash at the start that fades out in about half a second. For hits on a beat, camera flashes and sudden accents.
The screen edges glow red and pulse twice a second, like a heartbeat. For tension, love, fear or a racing pulse.
Pink and cyan bars jump across the picture now and then, like a broken signal. For tech, hacking or distorted moments.
Black bars sit at the top and bottom of the frame for a wide cinema shape. For a movie look in trailers and film scenes.
A cream instant-photo border surrounds the picture, thicker at the bottom. For memories, snapshots and travel photos.
Dark edges with light sprocket holes run down both sides, like a strip of film. For memories, old movies and slideshows.
White corner marks frame the picture, with a blinking red dot and REC at the top left. For camcorder, found-footage and vlog looks.
A glowing magenta neon tube outlines the picture and flickers now and then. For nightlife, music and cyberpunk looks.
Scan lines, a PLAY mark, a date stamp and a soft band rolling down the screen, like a VHS tape. For retro, home-video looks.
A single line of words whose font, size, color, style, entrance, loop and exit can all be changed. For any title, caption or label.

Text appears at once with no entrance animation. For plain captions that should not move.
Text fades in from transparent over 0.6 seconds. For calm, neutral entrances for titles and captions.
Text rises up a little from below while fading in. For gentle title and caption entrances.
Text drops down a little from above while fading in. For light, friendly title entrances.
Text scales up from small, overshoots slightly and settles. For lively, playful titles and stickers.
Text starts large and blurred, then shrinks and sharpens into place. For dramatic, punchy title reveals.
Text fades in from a heavy blur and comes into focus. For dreamy, soft title reveals.
Text slides in from the left while fading in. For lower thirds, captions and side entrances.
Text slides in from the right while fading in. For captions and side entrances that follow the first.
Text is revealed from left to right as if a mask sweeps across it. For clean, simple title reveals.
Text is revealed from left to right in a slow 1.2-second sweep, like typing. For captions and quotes.
Text slams in large and slightly tilted, then shrinks onto the frame like a rubber stamp. For emphatic words and approvals.
Text spins in from a quarter-turn while growing from small and fading in. For playful, energetic title entrances.
Text flips up from edge-on, as if turning toward the viewer, while fading in. For tech and stylish title entrances.
Text drops from above, bounces slightly past its place and settles. For cheerful, cartoon-style titles.
Text stays still while it shows, with no looping movement. For plain, steady captions.
Text drifts up and down slightly, in a slow loop. For light, floating titles and soft moods.
Text swells slightly in size and back, in a loop. For gentle emphasis on key words.
Text tilts a few degrees left and right, in a loop. For playful, cute emphasis on words.
Text trembles quickly from side to side, in a loop. For anger, fear, cold or shock.
Text slowly dims and returns to full brightness, in a loop. For calm, living text and soft glows.
Text rocks slowly a few degrees, like a hanging sign. For playful or casual titles.
Text flickers briefly now and then, like a faulty light. For neon, horror and electric titles.
Text disappears at once at the end with no exit animation. For plain captions that cut away.
Text fades out to transparent over half a second. For calm, neutral exits.
Text sinks down a little while fading out. For gentle exits, mirroring a rise-in.
Text lifts up a little while fading out. For light, airy exits.
Text shrinks to a small size while fading out. For quick, tidy exits.
Text blurs heavily while fading out. For dreamy, soft exits.
Text is wiped away from left to right as if a mask sweeps over it. For clean, simple exits.
Text grows large and blurred while fading out, as if flying past the camera. For dramatic exits.
Thin, widely spaced serif capitals rise gently into the center of the frame. For film titles, openings and quiet statements.
A big heavy white title pops in with a small overshoot. For strong headlines, openers and punchy statements.
Big letters drawn as outlines only, with no fill, slide in from the left. For modern, stylish headlines.
White letters with a pink glow flicker on like a neon sign. For nightlife, music and retro-futuristic titles.
A large title filled with a gold-to-pink gradient pops in with a small overshoot. For cheerful greetings and lively headlines.
Monospace words are typed out letter by letter with a blinking underscore cursor. For times, dates, notes and technical captions.
A small spaced-out chapter number sits above a large title that rises into place. For chapter cards and section breaks.
A quotation in white italic serif letters rises into the center. For quotes, reflections and quiet moments.
A bold name and a smaller role sit at the lower left with a thin line beside them, sliding in. For interviews and introductions.

A yellow four-pointed star twinkles, with a smaller one beside it. For magic, shine and highlights.

A red cross draws itself in two quick strokes. For wrong, rejected or cancelled points.
A red hand-drawn ring draws itself around something. For circling and highlighting a detail in a tutorial.
A yellow brush stroke draws itself left to right as an underline. For emphasizing a word or caption.
A red map pin drops in from above and settles with a small bounce. For marking a place on a map or in travel clips.
A thick yellow arrow pointing right nudges forward and back, repeating. For leading the eye or pointing to the next item.
